skill.name: cloud-architect
skill.description: Designs secure, resilient, and cost-aware cloud architectures across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Covers IaC, FinOps, migration planning, and multi-cloud strategy.
skill.summary: Guides multi-cloud architecture, IaC planning, FinOps, security, resilience, and migration strategy across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown prose and inline code formatting. No evidence found of prompt injection, command execution intent, data exfiltration, or reconnaissance behavior.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks mark the inline documentation path resources/implementation-playbook.md, not shell execution. The line only instructs the assistant to open a local reference file when examples are needed.
The line lists cloud quantum services and hybrid quantum-classical architectures as topic coverage. It does not request host discovery, OS enumeration, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Cloud planning often spans cost, security, resilience, and provider tradeoffs. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structure practical architecture guidance.
actual_capabilities: Recommends cloud services for AWS, Azure, and GCP workloads.
Plans infrastructure as code approaches with Terraform, OpenTofu, CDK, Bicep, and Pulumi.
Reviews cost optimization options using FinOps practices and provider pricing models.
Designs resilience patterns for multi-region, backup, and disaster recovery needs.
Covers security controls such as IAM, zero trust, encryption, compliance, and secrets management.
Structures migration, microservices, serverless, and event-driven architecture guidance.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance and cannot deploy cloud resources by itself.
Cost guidance depends on current provider pricing and user workload details.
Compliance recommendations need review by qualified legal and security teams.
It does not replace cloud provider documentation or production change controls.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Cloud Platform
use_cases.description: Create a secure baseline architecture with network, identity, deployment, monitoring, and cost controls.

use_cases.title: Optimize Cloud Spend
use_cases.description: Identify rightsizing, purchasing, tagging, and budget practices that reduce waste without harming reliability.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Cloud Migration
use_cases.description: Compare migration phases, service choices, risks, and rollback plans for an application portfolio.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this cloud architecture for cost, security, resilience, and operations risks: [describe current design].

prompt_templates.title: Select Cloud Services
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate service selection for one workload.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend AWS, Azure, or GCP services for this workload: [requirements]. Include tradeoffs, risks, and basic cost drivers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration planning for production systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration plan for [application portfolio]. Include dependencies, target architecture, testing, rollback, and operational readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Cloud Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced strategy across providers and regions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-cloud strategy for [business goal]. Include networking, identity, data, disaster recovery, FinOps, governance, and observability.

output_examples.input: Need an AWS web application architecture for unpredictable traffic.
output_examples.output: A serverless design using managed edge, compute, database, monitoring, and budget controls, with resilience and security notes.

output_examples.input: Our GCP costs are growing faster than usage.
output_examples.output: A FinOps review covering tagging, rightsizing, discounts, storage tiers, idle resources, alerts, and ownership practices.

output_examples.input: We must connect a data center to Azure for a phased migration.
output_examples.output: A hybrid cloud plan with connectivity options, identity integration, landing zone design, migration waves, and rollback checkpoints.

best_practices: Provide workload goals, constraints, traffic patterns, compliance needs, and budget targets before asking for a design.
Ask for tradeoffs between simplicity, cost, resilience, and operational effort.
Validate recommendations against current cloud provider documentation before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a final production design without sharing requirements and constraints.
Do not treat estimated costs as quotes from cloud providers.
Do not bypass security, compliance, or change approval processes based on generated guidance.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, GCP, and common multi-cloud architecture patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate infrastructure as code guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discuss Terraform, OpenTofu, CDK, Bicep, Pulumi, and native provider templates.

faq.question: Does it deploy cloud infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, review, and recommendation support for human-controlled implementation.

faq.question: Can it help reduce cloud costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest FinOps practices, rightsizing, discounts, budget controls, and cost allocation models.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated workloads?
faq.answer: It can outline security and compliance architecture patterns, but qualified reviewers must approve regulated designs.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
